implementation_notes: On Darwin a component is a bundle or dylib: Bundle(path:) plus load() (CFBundleLoadExecutable) maps it into the process and principalClass/classNamed(_:) resolves the component type, while the raw route is dlopen()/dlsym()/dlclose() with RTLD_LAZY or RTLD_NOW and the platform's reference-counted handles. The contract is a Swift protocol in a shared framework, but protocol witness tables and generics are only ABI-stable for libraries built with library evolution, so hosts normally resolve a small C or @objc factory entry point and cast the result to the protocol, with a version check. Bundle.unload() is deprecated and unsupported outside Darwin, and unloading code that still has live instances is unsafe, so Swift treats unlink as one-way: reconfiguration happens in a new process (or a plug-in point / XPC service). On Linux, dlopen from Glibc is used directly.
pitfalls: Bundle.unload() is deprecated and returns unsupported on non-Darwin platforms, and unloading a bundle with live instances is unsafe: loaded code stays mapped for the process lifetime, so hot replacement belongs in a new process.

Swift ABI stability covers the standard library and libraries built with library evolution; a component compiled against a different Swift version or an evolved contract can fail at the first protocol call, so keep the cross-boundary surface a versioned C/@objc factory.

classNamed(_:) goes through the Objective-C runtime (NSClassFromString), so pure Swift types that are not exposed to it must be reached through an exported factory symbol or the bundle's principal class.
